candidate.semantics: Run every ordinarily affordable repair at full production breadth. Only after the full-width selector returns no affordable repair, price one final suffix at 90% of the measured full-width upper cost and execute it at three-quarter candidate breadth. Stop repair after that suffix so its different-width cost profile cannot price another iteration.

basis.direct_observation: In the frozen 16-seed scale reference, resumed search at 750k spent 15,101 mean frames per compile but produced only 8 terminal register improvements and 6.22 aggregate internal-score points across 128 runs.
basis.association: Every fixed-ratio repair-width arm lost value when it narrowed an already-affordable suffix, including the post-target-only boundary.
basis.hypothesis: A narrower suffix can be useful only in the residual where full breadth is unaffordable and production would otherwise leave repair for lower-yield resumed work.
basis.pricing_limit: The 90% cost ratio is not a fitted cost model. It is a conservative policy price relative to the measured 11.65% mean episode-cost reduction in the completed repair-wide three-quarter arm.

mechanism_audit_n8.interpretation: The intervention is fully isolated. It does not cheapen or reorder any repair production could already afford; it converts a small amount of residual work into complete, often accepted suffixes. Their marginal gain density is low, so the expected authored-score effect is genuinely small.

interpretation: A fixed-width reduction is harmful when it replaces an affordable full-width repair, but useful as a strictly dominated-residue fallback. The gain is only 0.0028 canonical headline points and does not materially close the campaign target gap; promotion is justified by the predeclared statistical decision, exact isolation, unchanged validity, and nonnegative point estimate in every canonical case—not by effect size.
